verdicts.summary: Data side fixed as scoped. I confirmed the DB and yf_downloader stored ^VIX6M as 182 days while Cboe and config use 184. The DDL and yf comments called the indices a 'free proxy for VIX futures' and claimed a 0.5-2 pt gap; live data disproves that (2026-09-22: 29-day VX settled 17.36 vs ^VIX 14.21). Changes: tenor_days now comes from config.VIX_INDEX_TENOR_DAYS (plus new config.VVIX_TENOR_DAYS=30) in yf_downloader and in the new Cboe term-structure loader. insert_vix_term_structure enforces the config map, overriding a conflicting writer value with a warning. The DB migration set ^VIX6M to 184 on 4,137 rows. DDL and comments now describe spot-starting variance-swap indices. Real VX futures were ingested for option (b): 30,963 daily rows and 201 final settlements, read via get_vix_futures_curve. The calibrator side (term-index formula, tenor maps in joint/quintic/delta_hedger) belongs to other chains and is listed in cross_chain_requests.

verdicts.summary: I reproduced (a)-(g) offline on captures of the live endpoints taken 2026-10-12. SPX.json returns 403; with _SPX the old parser read 'Parsed 0 rows'; the VX parser raised TypeError on VX_2026-10-21.csv; _normalise_expiry_month(['V (Oct 2026)','Jan-24']) returned the input unchanged and '1-01'; BMonthEnd gave 2026-10-30; _load_vix_daily returned 0 without ever calling Yahoo. I rewrote cboe_downloader against the real endpoints. Option quotes come from _SPX.json/_VIX.json (the host now 307-redirects to cdn-api.cboe.com and requests follows it). The OCC symbol is parsed for root/expiry/right/strike, rows carry AM/PM settlement, mid is set only for two-sided quotes, and the snapshot is dated by the underlying's last_trade_time session, cross-checked against the clock. Added the index history CSVs (VIX, VIX9D, VIX3M, VIX6M, VVIX, VRO), the per-contract VX_<expiry>.csv and the daily settlement CSV, keyed (date, expiry_date). Settle is the mark; Cboe's 0 becomes NULL. The VX monthly-expiry rule handles holidays (2027-05-18). Final settlements use the contract expiry-day settle, with VRO only on monthly dates (see new finding). Pipeline: the Cboe->Yahoo fallbacks for VIX daily and option chains are now reachable, and Cboe is preferred for chains. The README row is for the docs stage.

Reproduced: the connection was still usable after `with`, and the tracked DB was in WAL mode. All access now goes through a contextlib connection that commits or rolls back and always closes. No WAL; the useless foreign_keys pragma is gone. init_database checkpoints and switches a WAL file to DELETE. init_database is read-only when the schema is current: I measured that even an empty write transaction bumps SQLite's header change counter, which would dirty the tracked file every time a DataPipeline is built. The committed DB is in DELETE mode, VACUUMed, and passes integrity_check.

new_findings.description: Cboe's VRO_History.csv is not a clean list of final settlements. From 2015 to 2020 it also holds rows for most other weekdays, carrying an earlier value forward (20.09 on every day 2019-01-11..22). The January 2019 contract actually settled at 18.87 per its own file; VIX opened at 18.08 that morning. Over 160 monthly contracts (2013-06..2026-09), the expiry-day settle equals VRO for 159.
new_findings.status: fixed: VRO is used only on standard monthly expiry dates, the contract file's expiry-day settle takes precedence, and disagreements are logged

new_findings.description: In Cboe's daily settlement CSV and per-contract files, an untraded weekly VX contract carries the same-month monthly's settle. On 2026-10-09, VX41/V6, VX43/V6, VX44/X6 and VX45/X6 all show 17.1186 (= VX/V6). These are not independent prices.
new_findings.status: fixed (mitigated): get_vix_futures_curve excludes weeklies by default and is_weekly is stored; the committed DB ingests monthly contracts only

new_findings.description: cdn.cboe.com/api/global/delayed_quotes/options/*.json now answers with a 307 redirect to cdn-api.cboe.com. 'SPX.json' is still 403 after the redirect; '_SPX.json' returns 200 (29,756 options, 56 expiries on 2026-10-12).
new_findings.status: fixed: _SPX/_VIX symbols; requests follows the redirect

new_findings.description: Cboe's index files carry values on NYSE holidays (VIX on 2026-01-19, 02-16, 06-19 and 07-03). The committed vix_daily holds 28 such holiday rows (e.g. 2022-05-30), and vix_term_structure has ^VIX on 2026-05-25. The dashboard's 'latest VIX' query can surface a holiday date.
new_findings.status: partially-fixed: the pipeline no longer ingests holiday rows and validate_sessions flags existing ones; existing rows are kept (no silent deletes)

new_findings.description: Cross-check of the committed DB against Cboe (tol 0.25): vix_daily lacks the 2026-06-12 session; ^VIX9D/^VIX3M/^VIX6M lack 2026-06-15..17; 8 ^VVIX sessions are missing inside the backtest window (2019-07-05, 2020-06-11, 2021-01-22, 2021-02-17, 2021-05-05, 2021-05-11, 2021-05-20, 2021-05-25). Within 2018-01-01..2025-03-24, ^VIX9D differs on 24 days, ^VVIX on 6 (max 2019-08-12: 105.31 vs 110.31) and ^VIX6M on 3.
new_findings.status: reported, not repaired (decision: hooks only); repair changes regime labels and backtest numbers

new_findings.description: idx_options_snap_date_und duplicated the prefix of the new natural key, and idx_vts_date duplicated the prefix of vix_term_structure's (date, ticker) primary key. Together they took about 2.0 MB of the tracked binary.
new_findings.status: fixed: dropped in the migration (query plans verified to use the remaining indexes)

new_findings.description: DataPipeline.daily_refresh always downloaded a fixed 5-day window. A DB that missed runs, such as the committed one that ends 2026-06-18, kept a permanent gap. This is the pipeline-path version of the ops 400-day-window time bomb.
new_findings.status: fixed: each table starts at its last stored session when that is earlier (one Yahoo request whatever the span); VX does the same with per-contract files

new_findings.description: Writers that supply time_to_expiry, such as cloud_refresh's (expiry - session).days/365, give AM-settled SPX contracts a T 6.5 hours too long. Yahoo's ^SPX chain mixes SPX (AM) and SPXW (PM) under one expiry date.
new_findings.status: fixed: stored T always follows time_to_settlement where the root/settlement is known

new_findings.description: Any write transaction, including a no-op CREATE IF NOT EXISTS, bumps SQLite's header change counter (bytes 24-27 and 92-95). Calling init_database() (every DataPipeline()) would therefore modify the git-tracked DB on every construction.
new_findings.status: fixed: init_database only reads when the schema is current

new_findings.description: quintic_calibrator._prepare_vix_term_structure takes each ticker's LAST row <= as_of independently, so tenors from different sessions are mixed when a sub-tenor is missing (e.g. 2026-06-15..17). It also hard-codes 91/182-day tenors. This is the defect C20 fixed in joint_calibrator.

JointCalibrator groups SPX rows by time_to_expiry (lines ~526, 831, 1102, 1333). With settlement-aware T, SPX (AM) and SPXW (PM) contracts expiring on the same date form two T groups, so nunique(time_to_expiry) double-counts expiries.

Under heavy machine load, the walk-forward tests (test_backtest_engine.py::TestWalkForward) with default OpenMP threads spent more than 14 minutes on one test. Single-threaded they take 16 s. The baseline run hit the same stall. This is not a code defect but makes CI time unpredictable.
new_findings.status: reported: the full suite was run with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 (743 passed, 24 skipped in 182 s)

cross_chain_requests.request: (1) Replace _VIX_TS_TENORS (91/182) with config.VIX_INDEX_TENOR_DAYS (9/30/93/184) and fit the indices with the spot-starting term-index formula; real VX futures are available via db.get_vix_futures_curve(as_of) (expiry_date, settle/price, days_to_expiry; monthlies only by default). (2) In _prepare_spx_surface call db.get_options_surface(as_of_date, 'SPX', max_age_sessions=0) or catch db.StaleDataError, instead of silently refitting an older chain. (3) Rows now carry root/settlement, and time_to_expiry is settlement-aware for new chains: SPX (AM) and SPXW (PM) on the same expiry date have T 6.5 h apart. Grouping by time_to_expiry (lines ~526, 831, 1102, 1333) therefore splits one expiry into two groups. Choose one root per expiry date (e.g. SPXW) or bucket by expiry date while pricing each row at its own T. (4) is_acceptable_calibration / latest_good_calibration_path: reject pickles whose spx_snapshot_date != spot session or with stale_spx_chain=True (key added by scripts/backfill_calibration_provenance.py), and require >= 3 SPX expiries (store n_spx_expiries).

_prepare_vix_term_structure: use config.VIX_INDEX_TENOR_DAYS instead of 91/182, and take all tenors from ONE session (the spot session), as joint_calibrator does. Today each ticker's last row <= as_of is taken independently, which mixes dates when a sub-tenor is missing. Pass max_age_sessions to get_options_surface.
VIX_TENORS has ^VIX6M = 182.0. Build it from config.VIX_INDEX_TENOR_DAYS (^VIX6M = 184; the DB now stores 184).

Replace the BT_START/BT_END literals with `from joint_vol_calibration.config import BT_START, BT_END` (same values: 2018-01-01, 2025-03-24). get_tbill_rates_series now returns continuously compounded rates (+4.5 bp mean in the window) plus a discount_yield column; the code selects ['rate'] explicitly, so no change is needed beyond re-running the backtest.
Import BT_START/BT_END from joint_vol_calibration.config instead of the '2025-03-24' literal at line ~41.
Import BT_END (and BT_START) from joint_vol_calibration.config instead of the literal at line ~508.

After downloads: database.export_market_partitions(since=start) and export_options_snapshot(spot_date, 'SPX'/'VIX'). (2) Use database.last_closed_session() instead of TODAY as the download end, and start = min(TODAY-400d, database.get_latest_date(table)) so no gap can open; or call DataPipeline().daily_refresh(). api_changes:
All existing public signatures still work; additions are keyword-optional.

database.py:
- NYSE calendar: nyse_holidays, nyse_sessions, is_nyse_session, previous_session, session_on_or_before, sessions_between, last_closed_session(now=None, cutoff=16:15 ET), quote_session(now=None), is_intraday(now=None), utc_iso. Constants NY_TZ, SESSION_OPEN, SESSION_CLOSE, CLOSE_DATA_CUTOFF. The clock is _utcnow(); tests monkeypatch it.
- Validation: validate_sessions(dates, start, end, label, log) -> {missing, extra}; find_bad_prints(df, label); cross_check_vix(reference_long_df, tol=0.25, start, end) -> discrepancy DataFrame (read-only).
- Option conventions: parse_occ_symbol, settlement_for_root, ROOT_SETTLEMENT (SPX/VIX/VIXW AM, SPXW PM), time_to_settlement(snapshot_date, expiry, settlement). time_to_expiry stored = minutes from the session's 16:00 ET close to 09:30 (AM) or 16:00 (PM) / 525,600 wherever the root is known. Legacy and unknown-root rows use whole days / 365, and a caller-supplied T is replaced when the settlement is known.
- VX: vx_monthly_expiry(year, month), vx_expiry_for_month('YYYY-MM').
  - vix_futures_daily is keyed (date, expiry_date) with columns expiry_month, symbol, is_weekly, open/high/low/close, settle, volume, open_interest, days_to_expiry, source. insert_vix_futures_daily merges column-wise and still accepts the legacy [date, expiry_month, close, ...] shape.
  - get_vix_futures_curve(as_of, include_weeklies=False) returns expiry_date, expiry_month, symbol, is_weekly, settle, close, price, days_to_expiry. Live contracts only; price = settle, else close.
  - vix_futures_settlements gains is_weekly and source.
- Rates: tbill_discount_to_cc(d, days=91). tbill_rates.rate is now continuously compounded and the new discount_yield column holds the raw ^IRX quote / 100. get_tbill_rates_series returns that extra column. Negative and zero rates are valid.
- Options:
  - insert_options_snapshot REPLACES the (snapshot_date, underlying) chain atomically under the UNIQUE key (snapshot_date, underlying, root, expiry, strike, right). New columns: root ('' = unrecorded), contract_symbol (yfinance contractSymbol accepted), settlement, underlying_price, quote_time, source.
  - get_options_surface(as_of, und, max_age_sessions=None) raises StaleDataError when the limit is exceeded and warns on any stale chain.
  - get_options_snapshot_dates(und=None), get_latest_date(table), redate_nonsession_snapshots().
- Tables: regime_labels is renamed classifier_predictions (insert/get_classifier_predictions). insert_regime_labels/get_regime_labels remain as deprecated aliases and get_regime_labels now validates start_date. spx_options is dropped.
- Persistence: MARKET_DIR, OPTIONS_DIR, MARKET_TABLES; export_market_partitions(root, tables, since), import_market_partitions(root, tables); export_options_snapshot(date, und, root, *, moneyness, max_years, two_sided_only), export_options_snapshots(root, since, **filters), import_options_snapshots(root, overwrite=False), options_snapshot_path.
- Schema: SCHEMA_VERSION=1 (PRAGMA user_version). init_database() migrates and is read-only on a current file. Every insert_* has a keyword warn_dropped=True.
- PARQUET_DIR is deprecated (nothing reads or writes it). _connect() was removed (private).

4. CROSS-SOURCE DISCREPANCIES, reported and NOT repaired (decision: hooks only; repairing moves labels and backtest numbers):
- ^VIX 2026-02-06 is Yahoo's 20.37, a copy of ^VIX3M; Cboe has 17.76. This affects both vix_daily and vix_term_structure.
- vix_daily lacks 2026-06-12. Sub-tenors are missing 2026-06-15..17.
- Inside the backtest window: ^VIX9D differs on 24 days, ^VVIX on 6 (2019-08-12: 105.31 vs Cboe 110.31), ^VIX6M on 3; 8 ^VVIX sessions are missing.
- vix_daily holds 28 NYSE-holiday rows; ^VIX in the term structure has 2026-05-25.
- tbill_rates lacks 2010-10-11 and 2016-11-11. Those are bond-market holidays, so this is legitimate.
- To repair, use database.cross_check_vix(cboe_downloader.download_vix_term_structure_history()) and insert the Cboe rows.

5. PERSISTENCE: the API exists but is not wired; see the cloud_refresh/workflow requests. Measured sizes: market partitions are a few KB per year per table. A full Cboe SPX chain is 848 KB per session and VIX 64 KB; filters (0.7-1.3 moneyness, <=1y, two-sided) only bring SPX down to ~680 KB, so roughly 230 MB a year on main if committed. Consider a data branch or release assets.

6. BEHAVIOUR CHANGES other chains will see:
- get_options_surface logs a warning when it returns a stale chain.
- New chains carry settlement-aware T, so AM and PM rows on the same expiry date have different T; the calibrator groups by T (see cross-chain request).
- DataPipeline.daily_refresh skips option snapshots while a session is trading.
- config no longer mkdirs; heston's MC cache needs its own mkdir (cross-chain).
- database.PARQUET_DIR is deprecated and kept only for test_lookahead.

7. ENVIRONMENT:
- No new pip dependencies. The NYSE calendar is rule-based (pandas holiday rules plus special closures through 2025-01-09); extend _NYSE_SPECIAL_CLOSURES if the exchange closes unexpectedly.
- zoneinfo uses the system tz database, which is present on the Ubuntu runners; Windows would need the tzdata package.
- The Cboe quote API now 307-redirects to cdn-api.cboe.com.

8. TEST RUNTIME: under heavy load, TestWalkForward with default OpenMP threads stalled for more than 14 minutes per test, and the baseline run hit the same stall. With OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 the full suite ran in 3 minutes. Recommend OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 for CI.
